title: Parts & Customisation
text:
Customisation
It is easy to customise the AniScope. Follow these steps:

Download OpenSCAD
Download this repository

From Github: click Code->Download Zip
From command line: git clone https://github.com/roaldarbol/AniScope.git

Open OpenSCAD
Open aniscope.scad
Enable the Customizer

Window -> Customizer

For the best experience, change Show descriptionto Description only.

text:
3. Diffuser

Orient the diffuser frame so the corner grooves face upward.
Flip it over—you’ll attach magnets to the bottom (the side now facing up).
Install magnets in the four corner holes using the same technique as Step 1.
Ensure polarity is correct: these magnets must attract the bottom piece’s magnets.

Checkpoint: Place the diffuser frame on the bottom piece. It should click into place magnetically and sit flat.

title: AniScope
text:
6. Camera
If using a USB camera with the X-mount top:

Attach the camera to the printed camera mount.
Slide the mount into the X-shaped slot on the top piece.
Secure with magnets or bolts as appropriate for your mount design.

If using a DSLR or external camera:

Position your tripod over the AniScope, looking down through the open top.
Adjust tripod height so the arena fills the camera’s field of view.

title: AniScope
text:
5. Assemble

Take the 4 MakerBeam 30 cm rails and 4 tapered bolts.
Screw a tapered bolt into each corner hole of the bottom piece. The rails should point upward.
Slide the diffuser frame down the rails from above.
On the sides with grooves, slide a standard bolt into the MakerBeam slot.
Adjust the diffuser to your desired height, then tighten the bolt with a nut to lock it in place.
(Optional) If using multiple diffusers, add them the same way at different heights.
Slide the arena down the rails and secure at the desired height.
Attach the top piece to the rail tops using the remaining tapered bolts.




Frame assembly

title: AniScope
text:
AniScope


 





A modular ethoscope for customised behavioural experiments with tiny animals.


Introduction
The AniScope is a modular, 3D-printed imaging arena for tracking small animals (insects, spiders, larvae, etc.). It provides uniform infrared backlighting, adjustable diffusion, and a stable camera mount—all in a compact, customisable package.


Features
Due to its modular design, AniScope is easy to modify:

Easy customization with the OpenSCAD Customizer
Create and use presets
Multiple arenas available
Goes hand-in-hand with BeeHive for electronics

title: Troubleshooting
text:
Troubleshooting








Problem
Possible Cause
Solution




LEDs don’t light up
Loose connector
Reopen connector, ensure contacts align, close firmly


Uneven lighting
Diffuser not taut; LED segment out
Check fabric tension; check each LED segment individually


Magnets won’t hold
Wrong polarity
Check orientation; you may need to remove and reinstall


Magnet fell out
Insufficient glue / pulled out before curing
Re-glue with fresh superglue; wait longer before testing


Camera image is blurry
Wrong focal distance; dirty lens
Adjust camera height; clean lens and diffuser


IR light not visible
LEDs not powered; camera can’t see IR
Check power; test with phone camera

title: AniScope
text:
4. Diffuser Fabric

Cut a piece of diffuser fabric approximately 20 cm × 15 cm (exact size is not critical; it just needs to cover the frame with ~2 cm overhang on each side).
Place the diffuser frame groove-side up.
Lay the fabric over the top.
On one short end, fold the fabric underneath and secure with 2 spare magnets on the underside.
Pull the fabric taut across the top.
Fold the opposite end underneath and secure with 2 more magnets.

Checkpoint: The fabric should be taut with no wrinkles. When held up to light, it should appear evenly translucent.

title: AniScope
text:
7. Power

Connect the LED strip’s power cable to your 12V supply.
Power on and verify all LEDs illuminate.
If using IR LEDs, you can verify operation with an IR camera (most cameras cannot see near-IR light).

title: AniScope
text:
2. LED Strips

Warning: When stripping waterproof strips, remove only the silicone coating, ensuring not to cut the strip itself.


Warning: Do not lift the metal contacts inside the click connectors. This causes loose connections that are difficult to fix.


Cut 4 segments from the LED strip roll, each 2 LEDs long (~10 cm). Cut only on the marked lines.
If using waterproof strips: carefully trim ~1 cm of silicone coating from each end to expose the contacts.
Open a corner connector by lifting the plastic flaps.
Insert one strip, matching + to + and − to −.
Close the flap firmly.
Repeat, connecting all four strips with three corner connectors to form a square.
Attach the end connector to one remaining strip end for power.
Place the LED strip assembly into the bottom piece’s floor.
Use small cable ties to secure across the connectors and in the middle of each segment.




LED strip assembly diagram


Checkpoint: Connect to 12V power briefly. All four strips should illuminate evenly - this may not be visible by eye, instead point an IR-sensitive camera at the strips to see whether they light up. If any strip is dim or off, check that connector’s contacts.

title: AniScope
text:
1. Magnets

Warning: Superglue bonds skin instantly. Wear gloves throughout this step, and have paper towels within reach to wipe up excess glue immediately.


Read this entire step before starting. Once glue is applied, you have only a few seconds to position the magnet.


Decide on magnet polarity
All magnets in upward-facing holes should have the same pole facing up. All magnets in downward-facing holes should have the opposite pole facing up. This ensures parts attach correctly later. The Magic Magnet Tool makes this easy by providing a tool for each.


Install each magnet

Place a magnet on the insertion tool (or hold carefully with gloved fingers), correct pole facing outward.
Apply a small drop of superglue into the hole.
Press the magnet firmly into the hole.
If using the tool, slide it sideways while holding the magnet in place with your other hand.
Immediately wipe away any excess glue with paper towel.
Repeat for all required holes.

Wait at least 5 minutes before bringing other magnets near—the glue needs time to cure, and magnetic attraction can pull magnets out of wet glue.



Magnet installation


Checkpoint: Magnets should sit flush with or slightly below the surface. Test with a loose magnet—it should snap firmly into place from ~1 cm away.



Attach magnets to diffuser

Orient the diffuser frame so the corner grooves face upward.
Flip it over—you’ll attach magnets to the bottom (the side now facing up).
Install magnets in the four corner holes using the same technique as Step 1.
Ensure polarity is correct: these magnets must attract the bottom piece’s magnets.

Checkpoint: Place the diffuser frame on the bottom piece. It should click into place magnetically and sit flat.

title: AniScope
text:
Notes and Tips

More diffusion needed? Add a second diffuser layer, or use a second diffuser frame with fabric at a different height.
Custom arena sizes: The design is parametric—see [link] to generate parts for different dimensions.
Filament choice: PLA works fine for most uses. PETG is more durable if you expect rough handling.
